name: Liam
profile: Liam is a 14-year-old who excels in mathematics and computer science but struggles significantly with open-ended assignments and group discussions. He finds eye contact uncomfortable, prefers concrete instructions, and becomes anxious when expectations are unclear. Liam has difficulty recognising when peers are frustrated with him and often continues behaviours that others find annoying.
challenges: Difficulty interpreting social cues from peers
Avoidance of subjects requiring creative writing or interpretation
goals: Complete open-ended assignments with reduced anxiety
Improve peer relationships through increased social understanding
Develop self-advocacy skills for requesting clarification
Build confidence in subjects beyond STEM

recommendedEBPs.title: Structured Work Systems
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Breaks ambiguous assignments into clear, sequential steps

recommendedEBPs.title: Social Skills Training
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Explicitly teaches recognition and interpretation of social cues

recommendedEBPs.title: Peer-Mediated Instruction
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Structures positive peer interactions with trained classmates

recommendedEBPs.title: Video Modeling
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Demonstrates expected behaviours in social and academic contexts

implementation.structuredWork: Teachers provided step-by-step assignment sheets with specific success criteria and examples. Open-ended tasks were scaffolded with choices rather than complete freedom.
implementation.socialSkills: Liam met weekly with school counsellor to practise interpreting facial expressions, tone of voice, and body language using video examples and role-play.
implementation.peerMediation: Two volunteer classmates were trained to include Liam in group work, provide gentle cues, and check in about task requirements.
implementation.videoModeling: Liam watched short videos showing appropriate group work behaviours, turn-taking in conversation, and asking for help.

outcomes: Liam completed three open-ended English assignments with teacher-provided structure
Peer conflicts reduced significantly after 8 weeks of social skills work
Liam successfully self-advocated for clarification in geography class
Peer-mediated group work resulted in positive experience in science project
Teachers report Liam appears more relaxed and engaged in non-STEM subjects
reflections: Initially, subject teachers felt providing structure was 'lowering standards', but came to recognise that clarity about expectations allowed Liam to demonstrate his actual ability. The peer-mediation component was surprisingly powerful - having trained peer support reduced Liam's reliance on adult intervention. Social skills training needed to be very explicit and example-based; abstract social advice was unhelpful.

context.supportLevel: Tier 2 - resource teacher support and counsellor access
